verdict.rationale: Sentry documents ingesting OpenTelemetry traces and logs over OTLP, either directly from an OTel SDK or through the OpenTelemetry Collector. That means OTel-instrumented code can be pointed at Sentry or at another backend without re-instrumenting. However, the evidence covers only traces and logs. It also suggests Sentry's richer features rely on its own SDK, with an OTLP integration only bridging trace context. missing for 10: documented OTLP ingestion of metrics and errors/exceptions, evidence that full Sentry functionality works from pure OTel instrumentation without the Sentry SDK, and independent hands-on corroboration of backend switching.

support.subject: As an SRE, I can instrument once with open standards and switch backends without re-instrumenting my code

citations.quote: Sentry can ingest OpenTelemetry traces and logs via OTLP endpoints, either directly from an OTel SDK or through a pipeline tool like the OpenTelemetry Collector.
to share trace context between Sentry and OTel
